section: Satellite Symposium: Complement and the Brain [1st Sep 2026]
text:
Satellite Symposium: Complement and the Brain [1st Sep 2026]
We are delighted to host a satellite symposium on ‘Complement and the Brain’, running in parallel with the Teaching Day (on Tuesday 1st September 2026). This symposium will focus on the emerging roles of complement in neuroinflammation and neurodegenerative diseases, with presentations ranging from fundamental mechanisms to therapeutic developments.
In the late afternoon of the satellite symposium the keynote will be delivered by Professor Baljit Khakh (Centre Director & Research Division Lead, UK Dementia Research Institute).
We are grateful to the UK DRI for supporting this event.
Registration is open to all (including those not attending the main conference).

title: Travel
text:
Cardiff is easy to reach from across Europe and beyond. Whether you’re flying in from the US, mainland Europe, or further afield, here’s how to plan your journey:



Direct flights to Cardiff (CWL) via Amsterdam and Dublin.
Alternatively, fly into London Heathrow (LHR), Bristol (BRS), or Birmingham (BHX) – each with easy rail links to Cardiff.





Fly to London Heathrow (LHR) or to Cardiff via Amsterdam or Dublin.
From Heathrow, take the Heathrow Express to London Paddington Station, then a direct train to Cardiff or the Elizabeth Line to Reading and train from there (each ~2.5 hours total).
ternative London airports:
Gatwick (LGW): Gatwick Express to Victoria Station → Tube to Paddington → train to Cardiff.
London City (LCY): DLR and Tube to Paddington.
Stansted (STN) and Luton (LTN): Rail to central London, then Paddington → Cardiff.

All major airports are also served by National Express and Megabus coaches to Cardiff.




Excellent connections via Doha, Dubai, or Istanbul into London or Birmingham.
Continue to Cardiff by train.






From 2025, visitors from the EU, US, Canada, Australia and others will need a UK Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA). Current fee: £16 per person. Apply online here: https://www.gov.uk/eta




Your passport must be valid for the full duration of your stay in the UK.
No visa is required for short visits from many countries – check UK entry requirements.




EU Entry/Exit System (EES)
If travelling onwards to Europe after EMCHD2026, be aware of new biometric checks and longer border times for non-EU nationals.
More on EES here: https://www.government.nl/topics/holidays-and-travels/ees



Cardiff is a walkable city, with most venues, hotels, restaurants, and attractions within easy walking distance. Our conference venue and social events are all located in the city centre, making it easy to get around on foot. Cardiff is well-connected by train and bus to all major UK cities. For more information on how to get here, please refer to the link: https://www.hhcardiff.ac.uk/visit/directions

QuidelOrtho





QuidelOrtho Specialty Products Group (SPG) is a well-established name in immune system monitoring, assays for the assessment of complement activation and biosafety and cytotoxicity testing. QuidelOrtho SPG’s MicroVue product portfolio includes ELISAs, multiplex, antibodies, proteins, depleted sera, normal human serum, cobra venom factor and special reagents for all your complement research needs.

title: Sponsors
text:
Compvide





Compvide is a Seattle-based biotechnology company focused on advancing complement system diagnostics and immune monitoring technologies. The company is developing CIMED™ (Complement Inhibition Monitoring & Efficacy Determination), a novel platform designed to measure complement pathway activity, complement deficiencies, and complement drug efficacy under physiologic, high-serum conditions. Unlike conventional assays that rely on highly diluted serum, CIMED enables functional assessment of the alternative, lectin, and classical complement pathways in conditions that better reflect human biology.
Compvide’s technology supports translational research, complement drug development, complement deficiency screening, and patient monitoring applications, with potential use across autoimmune, renal, inflammatory, infectious, and hematologic diseases. The platform is being developed for both Research Use Only (RUO) applications and future clinical diagnostic implementation.
The company collaborates with leading scientists, pharmaceutical partners, and manufacturing organizations to accelerate innovation in complement therapeutics and diagnostics. Compvide’s mission is to bridge the gap between complement-targeted therapies and real-time functional immune monitoring, helping advance precision medicine in complement-related diseases.
Learn more by visiting compvide.com

title: Awards
text:
We are grateful to the Lambris Family for their longstanding support of early-career researchers through the Lambris Training Award within ICS, and for extending this support to the ECN meeting at EMCHD2026 for the first time.





This award will be presented for the first time at EMCHD 2026 in Cardiff. The Lambris Complement Training Award aims to recognize and support an outstanding early-career researcher who shows exceptional promise in becoming a leading investigator in complement research. The award includes a Certificate of Award and a honorarium of €2,500.
To apply for the award, you must:

Be registered for EMCHD 2026
Have submitted an abstract
Follow the guidelines available here: https://www.ecomplement.org/activities/lambris-complement-training-award
Note that nominations may be suggested and submitted by any member of the ECN; self-applications are not accepted
The nomination deadline is July 15, 2026. Please send your application to Mihály Józsi at mihaly.jozsi@ttk.elte.hu.

title: Awards
text:
Eligibility
• Early-Career Researchers who have published a paper focussing on the complement system.
• The published work was (or will be) included in your PhD thesis.
• Registered as a member of ECCO. (Membership is free: https://bit.ly/ECCOmembership).
• The applicant is registered for the 20th European Meeting on Complement in Human Disease in Cardiff, Wales.
Applications should include:

Short Curriculum Vitae (1 page).
Motivation letter (1 – 2 pages).
The published article (PDF version).

The motivation letter should address:
• What are the key findings/outcomes of the paper?
• What was your contribution to the Journal Article?
• Why did you choose a PhD project in complement research?
• Which challenges did you have to overcome for your PhD?
• Why should you get the ECCO PhD Journal Article Award?

title: Awards
text:
Application Deadline
The application deadline is 12th July 2026. The ECCO committee will select the awardee, who will be notified of the decision by early August 2026.
The application documents (as one single pdf) must be submitted electronically to ecco@complement.org.
Re-Submissions from past applications are welcome and will be accepted.
Feel free to contact the ECCO committee (ecco@complement.org) for any questions regarding the ECCO PhD Journal Article Award.

title: ECR Events
text:
Early-career researchers (ECRs) are a key component of the European complement network, and we are keen to welcome you all to capital of Wales for EMCHD26. Organised in collaboration between the local organising committee and Early-Career Complementologists (ECCO) we have a selection of great activities to help foster relationships between ECRs and make sure ECRs are at the forefront of the meeting.

Networking Like A Boss! – Date 2026-09-03
Join our special networking event to connect with several invited high-profile figures in the field of complement, who will come and introduce themselves to you!


ECR social/Pub quiz hosted at Tiny Rebel – Date 2026-09-03, 19:00 start
A fun quiz (non-science-based) hosted by ECCO in a popular bar run by the Welsh craft brewery Tiny Rebel located in the centre of Cardiff (CF10 1DD). Limited spaces are available (60) so please indicate during registration that you wish to attend. Food, drinks and prizes will be included!







5th annual ECCO PhD journal article award and talk – Conference session
5th annual ECCO PhD Journal Article Award, sponsored by the European Complement Network (ECN), offering a prize of €500. Applications for this award will be opening soon, and the winner will be announced and be invited to deliver an oral presentation during the ECMHD meeting.
If you need more information, queries or suggestions for additional activities/events, don’t hesitate to email emchd2026@cardiff.ac.uk. We look forward to welcoming you to Cardiff for an engaging and productive EMCHD meeting.
